name.text: Question 5 - Area Between Curves [Broken wrong extremes of integration]

questiontext.text:
Determine the area of the region bounded by \({@expr1@}, \, {@expr2@}, \, y={@y_1@}\) and \(y={@y_2@}\)

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Here is a sketch of the bounded region we want to find the area.

[[jsxgraph]] const board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-3, 5, 10, -3], axis: true }); // Plot functions only up to the mutual intersections var function1 = board.create('functiongraph', ['sqrt(x-3)', 4, 3], {name: 'x=3+y^2', withlabel: true}); var function2 = board.create('functiongraph', ['-sqrt(x-3)', 3, 7]); var function3 = board.create('functiongraph', ['-2', 7, -2]); var function5 = board.create('functiongraph', ['-sqrt(-x+2)', -2, 2], {name: 'x=2-y^2', withlabel: true}); var function6 = board.create('functiongraph', ['sqrt(-x+2)', 2, 1]); var function4 = board.create('functiongraph', ['1', 1, 4]); // The elements can be FunctionGraphs or Pairs of coordinates (encoding points) // properties is a dictionary of properties for the generated function. function make_filled_curve(board, element_list, properties) { var curve = board.create('curve', [[], []], properties); curve.updateDataArray = function () { this.dataX = []; this.dataY = []; for (const element of element_list) { if (Array.isArray(element)) { // Add the point to the curve this.dataX.push(element[0]); this.dataY.push(element[1]); } else { // Copy all points from function this.dataX = this.dataX.concat(element.points.map(p => p.usrCoords[1])); this.dataY = this.dataY.concat(element.points.map(p => p.usrCoords[2])); } } // Close the loop this.dataX.push(this.dataX[0]); this.dataY.push(this.dataY[0]); }; board.update(); } // Plot different filled functions make_filled_curve(board, [function1, function2, function3, function5, function6, function4], { strokeWidth: 3, fillColor: 'green', fillOpacity: 0.3 }); [[/jsxgraph]]

It is clear from the graph that the curves \({@expr1@}\) and \({@expr1@}\) with lines \(y={@y_1@}\) and \(y={@y_2@}\) are really bounded by the region indicated in green colour, (in between the blue and red curves).

Recall: Area between two curves with respect to the y-axis.

If \(f(y)\) and \(g(y)\) are continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(f(y) < g(y)\) for all \(y\) in \([a, b]\), then

\(Area = \displaystyle \int_{a}^{b} [g(y) -f(y)] dy\)

In other words if the area of the region bounded by \(x=f(y), \, x= g(y), \, y=a \, \text{and} \,y=b\) exists then the area if given by

\(Area = \displaystyle \int_{a}^{b} | f(y) -g(y) | dy\)

Therefore,

\( \begin{align} A &= \displaystyle \int_{{@y_1@}}^{{@y_2@}} \left( {@rhs(expr1)@}-({@rhs(expr2)@}) \right) dy \\ &= \displaystyle \int_{{@y_1@}}^{{@y_2@}} \left( {@(rhs(expr1)-rhs(expr2))@}\right) dy \\ &= \displaystyle \left[{@area_func@}\right]_{{@y_1@}}^{{@y_2@}} \\ &= {@ta@} \end{align} \)
